text: The top of Lesson 53's architecture needs exactly two linked services before a single row of data moves: one pointing at the on-premises SQL Server through the self-hosted IR from Chapter Seven, and one pointing at the ADLS Gen2 raw zone.

Notice this already satisfies two Lesson 53 requirements at once. ConnectVia handles the on-premises bridge, and the connection string is a Key Vault reference, not a raw string — security genuinely isn't something bolted on at the end here, it's built into the very first linked service you write.

With connections in place, the Copy activity itself is genuinely simple. The sqlReaderQuery filters to exactly yesterday's orders — a real, deliberate choice. Copying the entire sales table every single night would work today, but it would only get slower and more wasteful as Northwind's order history keeps growing.

The sink is Parquet, not CSV, for three concrete reasons. Columnar storage lets the mapping data flow in Lesson 56 read only the handful of columns it actually needs. Schema travels embedded in the file itself. And it's natively compatible with Spark and OneLake, the same format Lesson 45 covered as the backbone of one copy of data in Fabric.

Before moving on, the bar for this stage is genuinely concrete and testable: run the pipeline manually, confirm exactly one new Parquet file lands with only yesterday's orders, and check its schema through Preview data. Not probably works — verified.

Two linked services, one deliberately filtered Copy activity, and a real reason behind every choice made. Next: Add Control Flow and Error Handling — what genuinely happens tonight if the on-premises server simply isn't reachable.
